9	---
10	
11	# Agent-Native Plans
12	
13	Agent-Native Plans is structured visual planning mode for coding agents. Build
14	the plan you would normally write in Markdown, but as a scannable document with
15	editable blocks mixed in: inline diagrams, code snippets,
16	open questions, and an optional top visual review area (wireframe canvas, live
17	prototype, or both in tabs). Architecture and backend plans stay document-only;
18	UI and product plans start with the top canvas/prototype (the Visual Surface
19	Choice section owns that rule).
20	
21	`/visual-plan` is the packaged command and main entry point. Choose the review
22	mode from the task: UI-first when the work is primarily product UI and review
23	should start with screens, prototype-first when review should start with a
24	functional live prototype, design-first when review needs full-fidelity branded
25	screens, or visual-intake when the user explicitly wants a questionnaire before
26	planning. When a Codex, Claude Code, Markdown, or pasted plan already exists,
27	`/visual-plan` uses that source plan as the starting point and builds the review
28	surface from it instead of starting over.
29	
30	## When To Use
31	
32	Create or adapt a visual plan whenever the plan would be better as a reviewable
33	artifact than a chat paragraph. This includes modest work such as a single UI
34	surface with states, a small workflow, a before/after product change, or a
35	component/API/data-shape decision that needs alignment, plus larger multi-file,
36	ambiguous, long-running, risky, or UI-heavy work. Use it when architecture /
37	data flow / UI direction / options / open questions would benefit from inline
38	diagrams or structured blocks, when the user needs to react to a direction
39	before you implement, or when an existing text plan needs a richer review
40	surface.
41	
42	## Plan Discipline
43	
44	- **Gate thoughtfully.** A visual plan is a richer review surface, not only a
45	  tool for giant projects. Use it when the user needs to see, compare, comment
46	  on, or approve a direction before code, even for a modest UI/state/workflow
47	  change. Skip it for truly trivial, unambiguous work — typos, one-line fixes, a
48	  single well-specified function, anything whose diff you could describe in one
49	  sentence — and just make the change. Never pad a plan with filler and never
50	  ship a single-step plan.
51	- **Research before you draft.** Read the real files, actions, schema, and
52	  patterns first; name actual files, symbols, and data shapes instead of
53	  inventing them. Check existing `actions/` before proposing endpoints and prefer
54	  named client helpers over raw fetch. Delegate wide exploration to a sub-agent.
55	  Lead with reuse: for each step, name what it reuses — existing actions, schema,
56	  components, helpers — before what it adds, so the plan explains the genuinely new
57	  delta instead of redescribing what already exists.
58	- **Decide the hard-to-reverse bets first.** For non-trivial backend, data, or API
59	  work, sketch where the feature is headed, then call out the decisions that are
60	  expensive to undo once data or callers depend on them — wire format, public ids,
61	  data-model shape, auth and ownership boundaries — and get those right in the plan
62	  even if most of the feature ships later. Then scope to the smallest first cut that
63	  proves the approach without foreclosing it, stating both what is in and what is
64	  explicitly deferred.
65	- **Keep examples at the right altitude.** When the user's idea is a broad
66	  framework, product, or operating-model change, do not collapse it into the
67	  first concrete example, provider, or sync path they mention. Separate the core
68	  abstraction from motivating examples and app/provider adapters. Use examples
69	  to make the plan legible, but label them as examples unless they are the whole
70	  requested scope.
71	- **Publish standalone plans.** If the user pasted, referenced, or already has a
72	  Codex / Claude Code / Markdown plan, treat it as source material, but rewrite
73	  the published plan as a clean standalone proposal. Preserve the source plan's
74	  useful intent and codebase facts, label inferred visuals as inferred, and avoid
75	  revision language such as "preserve the prior plan", "do not drop the old
76	  idea", "unlike the previous version", or "this revision changes...". A reader
77	  who never saw the chat or earlier drafts should understand the plan.
78	- **Make the first read concrete.** If the plan is meant to be shared with
79	  someone outside the chat, or if the concept is abstract, lead near the top with
80	  one concrete product example before mode tables, architecture, or roadmaps. For
81	  UI-capable concepts, that usually means a top-canvas app state that shows the
82	  real user workflow in product terms. Do not rely on phrases that only make
83	  sense in conversation, and do not frame the plan as "not the old idea"; state
84	  the positive model directly.
85	- **Planning is read-only.** Make no source edits while building or reviewing the
86	  plan. Start editing only after the user approves the direction.
87	- **Clarify vs. assume.** Do not ask how to build it — explore and present the
88	  approach and options in the plan. Ask a clarifying question only when an
89	  ambiguity would change the design and you cannot resolve it from the code; use
90	  the host agent's normal ask-user-question flow and batch 2-4 high-leverage
91	  questions before finalizing. Do not call `create-visual-questions` from
92	  `/visual-plan`. Otherwise state the assumption explicitly and proceed, and
93	  keep anything unresolved in the plan's single bottom `question-form` Open
94	  Questions block. For complex plans, do a final open-question pass before
95	  handoff: if a decision would affect architecture, scope, UX, data shape, or
96	  rollout, either decide it in the plan with rationale or put it in that bottom
97	  form with a recommended default.
98	- **The plan is the approval gate.** After surfacing it, ask the user to review
99	  and approve before you write code, and name which files/areas the work touches.
100	  Presenting the plan and requesting sign-off is the approval step — do not ask a
101	  separate "does this look good?" question.
102	- **The document is the source of truth, not the chat.** When scope shifts,
103	  update the plan with `update-visual-plan` rather than only changing course in
104	  chat, and make the updated document stand alone. Do not describe the update as
105	  a correction to an earlier draft inside the plan itself. Re-read the approved
106	  plan before major steps.
107	
108	## Create A Structured Agent-Native Plan — Never Inline
109	
110	The deliverable is ALWAYS a structured Agent-Native Plan, not a chat-only plan.
111	The hosted Plan MCP connector (`plan` server, or legacy `agent-native-plans`) is
112	the default collaboration and commenting surface; it is not a reason to reject
113	the planning pattern as an external dependency or rented layer. Plans are
114	portable source artifacts (`plan.mdx`, optional `canvas.mdx` /
115	`prototype.mdx`, JSON, and HTML export), and ownership-sensitive workflows can
116	use local-files mode or a self-hosted/custom Plan app URL without abandoning the
117	skill's review discipline. Do not advise the user to skip `/visual-plan` because
118	the default surface is hosted; choose the right Plan mode for the user's
119	ownership, privacy, sharing, and branding needs.
120	
121	By default, create the plan via the Plan MCP connector. NEVER hand the plan over
122	as inline chat content — no Markdown prose, ASCII sketch, table, or fenced
123	wireframe. Some clients lazy-load connector tools through a deferred tool
124	registry instead of showing the `plan` namespace upfront; before declaring the
125	connector missing, search/load tools with the host's discovery surface
126	(`tool_search` when available) for `create_visual_plan`, `create_ui_plan`, or
127	`get_plan_blocks`, then use the Plan MCP tools it exposes. If the connector's
128	tools are still missing after discovery, do NOT fall back to inline output: the
129	usual cause is a connector that did not finish connecting this session (it
130	registers zero tools), not auth. Stop and give the user the exact restore step
131	for their current client: in Codex/Codex Desktop run
132	`npx -y @agent-native/core@latest reconnect https://plan.agent-native.com --client codex`
133	and start a new Codex session; in Claude Code run `/mcp` and choose
134	Authenticate/Reconnect (or run the same reconnect command with
135	`--client claude-code` and restart Claude). Auth is stored per client
136	config/session, so one client's reconnect does not make another running client
137	load tools. Never reinstall from scratch just to fix auth. Publish once the tool
138	is reachable. Local-files privacy mode (after Tool Guidance) is the exception.
139	
140	## Core Workflow
141	
142	1. Follow the host agent's normal planning flow: inspect the codebase, delegate
143	   wide exploration when useful, gather the info needed, and ask native
144	   clarifying questions as needed before generating the plan. If a source plan
145	   already exists, gather its exact text from the user's paste, a referenced
146	   file, or recent visible agent context; do not invent source text.
147	2. Call `get-plan-blocks` for the authoritative block catalog — do not author
148	   from memorized tags. Then call the mode-matched create tool:
149	   `create-visual-plan` for document-first plans (architecture, backend, data,
150	   refactor, API), `create-ui-plan` for UI-first plans, `create-prototype-plan`
151	   for prototype-first plans, `create-plan-design` for design-first plans,
152	   `create-visual-questions` only when the user explicitly asks for a visual
153	   intake questionnaire. When a source plan already exists,
154	   pass it as `planText` and preserve the original plan's useful intent while
155	   producing a standalone plan document, not a revision memo.
156	3. For UI/product plans, compose the top canvas first with the primary
157	   wireframes and annotated states, then write the document with native blocks
158	   (see `references/canvas.md` and `references/document-quality.md`). For
159	   broad product architecture plans with a user-facing implication, add a
160	   concrete "what this looks like in the app" visual before the abstract
161	   architecture or mode tables. Keep the document close to the standalone
162	   Markdown plan the agent would normally output. If an existing plan was
163	   provided, carry forward the right facts and decisions without referring to
164	   the previous draft or explaining how this version differs. For non-visual
165	   plans, skip the top visual surface (Visual Surface Choice below owns the rule)
166	   and put `diagram`, `data-model`,
167	   `api-endpoint`, `diff`, `file-tree`, `code`, and `annotated-code` blocks
168	   directly next to the relevant prose.
169	   Wide document layout is renderer-owned and intentionally allowlisted: only
170	   literal code-review surfaces (`diff`, `annotated-code`) and `tabs` blocks
171	   with vertical orientation or diff-like children break out wider than prose.
172	   Keep `api-endpoint`, `openapi-spec`, `data-model`, `json-explorer`,
173	   `wireframe`, question, and `custom-html` blocks in normal document flow unless
174	   their own renderer says otherwise.
175	4. Surface the returned Plans link or inline MCP App and ask the user to review.
176	   Always include the actual URL in chat so the next step is a click in CLI or
177	   other text-only hosts. When the host exposes an embedded browser/preview panel
178	   and a tool can open arbitrary URLs there, open the returned plan URL
179	   automatically for convenient review — a convenience and smoke test, never the
180	   only handoff or the access
181	   model. Plans should load out of the box for the local agent and local browser
182	   session; if a signed-in embedded browser cannot read a local plan that an
183	   anonymous/tool check can read, fix the app/action ownership or access path
184	   rather than patching one plan by hand. For high-stakes plans (architecture,
185	   backend, data, multi-file, or risky), also kick off the self-review pass in
186	   **Self-Review Before Handoff** while the user reads, instead of blocking the
187	   handoff on it.
188	5. Call `get-plan-feedback` before editing, after review, after any long pause,
189	   and before the final response. Treat `anchorDetails`, resolver intent, recent
190	   review events, and any focused screenshots from browser handoff as the source
191	   of truth for exactly what changed and exactly what each comment points at.
192	6. Apply changes with `update-visual-plan`, preferring targeted `contentPatches`.
193	   Treat the top-level `content` payload as a full replacement, not a merge; do
194	   not send a partial `content` object to add a canvas or one block. If a full
195	   replacement is unavoidable, first read the complete plan source/content, carry
196	   forward every existing block and visual surface, and verify the source/export
197	   afterward so the document body was not truncated. When the user wants
198	   source-control friendly edits, use `patch-visual-plan-source` against the MDX
199	   files instead of regenerating the plan.
200	7. Export with `export-visual-plan` only when the user wants a shareable receipt
201	   or repo-check-in artifacts.
202	
203	## Self-Review Before Handoff
204	
205	For high-stakes plans — architecture, backend, data-model, migration, multi-file,
206	or otherwise risky work — run one adversarial self-review pass before treating the
207	plan as final. Skip it for small, UI-only, or single-decision plans where the cost
208	outweighs the value. Keep the pass cheap and non-blocking:
209	
210	- **Surface the plan first, review concurrently.** Post the link and let the user
211	  start reading, then run the review in parallel — never make the user wait on it.
212	- **Review the written plan; do not re-research.** Critique the plan text and its
213	  own blocks. The grounding was already done while drafting, so the review checks
214	  the output instead of re-exploring the repo.
215	- **Spawn one skeptical reviewer** whose only job is to find what is weak, missing,
216	  or wrong — not to praise. Point it at: hard-to-reverse decisions made implicitly
217	  or not at all (wire format, public ids, data-model shape, auth, ownership); steps
218	  not anchored in real files or symbols; a menu of options where the plan should
219	  commit to one; obvious missing decisions ("what happens when X?", "why not Y?");
220	  and padding or single-step filler.
221	- **Fix vs. ask.** Apply clear-cut fixes yourself with `update-visual-plan`
222	  `contentPatches` — vague non-goals, unanchored claims, an obvious missing
223	  decision. Route genuine judgment calls back to the user instead: add them to the
224	  bottom `question-form` Open Questions block or batch them into the normal
225	  ask-user-question flow. Do not silently decide them.
226	- **Do not surprise the user mid-read.** On a large plan, apply the patches before
227	  the editor loads; otherwise note briefly that a self-review is running so the
228	  plan changing under them is expected. When you next respond, summarize what the
229	  review changed and what it surfaced for the user to decide.
230	
231	## Visual Surface Choice
232	
233	Choose the surface before creating the plan or after reading the source plan. Do
234	not add visual chrome by default:
235	
236	For UI/product plans, the top canvas is usually the primary review surface. Put
237	the first meaningful wireframes there, not buried as document-body blocks. Use
238	multiple canvas artboards when states matter, such as the default view, an
239	overflow menu or popover, a side panel, loading, or error. Put short annotations
240	beside frames with `targetId` plus `placement`; keep implementation details,
241	tradeoffs, file maps, data contracts, risks, and verification in the document
242	body below the canvas.
243	
244	When the user asks for a flow, storyboard, journey, wireframe, canvas, or "what
245	this looks like", treat that as a canvas-first request. Make one artboard per
246	user-visible state, connect only adjacent transitions, and use short canvas
247	annotations for the product notes. Do not substitute a document-body `diagram`
248	block for the requested storyboard just because HTML diagrams are faster to
249	write; diagrams belong below the canvas for backend mechanics, architecture, or
250	data-flow explanation.
251	
252	Keep product wireframes and explanatory/meta diagrams separate. Start with pure
253	screens that look like the app state under discussion, without callout prose or
254	architecture notes embedded inside the UI. Put arrows, labels, contracts, data
255	flow, and mode explanations in separate annotations, separate canvas diagrams,
256	or the document body.
257	
258	When the plan touches an existing app, inspect the current shell/components
259	before drawing. The first artboard should look like the real app at the same
260	density: existing sidebars, toolbar placement, overflow menus, app chrome, and
261	framework agent chrome stay in their real places. Model secondary surfaces as
262	separate states, such as a top-right overflow popover, sheet, panel, loading
263	state, or separate AgentSidebar, rather than inventing a permanent inspector or
264	folding framework chrome into the product UI.
265	
266	- **No visual surface** for architecture-only, backend-only, data migration,
267	  copy-only, or otherwise non-visual plans. Do not use the top canvas for
268	  architecture diagrams, dependency maps, file plans, API contracts, or
269	  data-flow-only reviews. Use a strong document with local inline diagrams
270	  only when relationships need a visual explanation, usually one spatial diagram
271	  per recommendation or decision. Prefer grouped regions, layers, quadrants,
272	  matrices, or before/after panels over a single-axis chain unless the
273	  relationship is truly sequential.
274	- **Canvas only** for one static screen, a before/after comparison, a component
275	  state, a small popover, or a visual direction that does not require clicking.
276	  Put those wireframes in `content.canvas` and omit `content.prototype`.
277	- **Canvas + prototype** for multi-step UI flows, onboarding, wizards,
278	  review/approval flows, navigation changes, or anything where the reviewer
279	  needs to operate the behavior. Keep the static wireframes in
280	  `content.canvas`, add the aligned functional prototype in
281	  `content.prototype`, and rely on the top visual tabs to switch between them.
282	- **Prototype-first** when the user asks to operate the UI or when interaction is
283	  the main question. Use `create-prototype-plan`, which still preserves static
284	  mocks where useful.
285	
286	For mixed canvas + prototype plans, reuse the same real labels, app statuses,
287	and screen ids across both surfaces. The canvas is the inspectable static reference;
288	the prototype is the interactive version of that same flow, not a separate
289	design direction.
290	
291	## Wireframe quality — read `references/wireframe.md`
292	
293	UI recap/plan wireframes must meet a strict quality bar — full-width chrome,
294	pinned bottom bars, real product content, before/after comparability, the right
295	`surface` preset, `--wf-*` tokens instead of hex, and no `<html>`/`<style>`/font
296	tags. Before authoring ANY wireframe / `<Screen>` / `WireframeBlock`, READ
297	`references/wireframe.md` in this skill directory — it is the single source of
298	truth for HTML wireframe quality, shared word for word with `/visual-plan`
299	and `/visual-recap`. Do not author wireframes from memory.
300	
301	## Canvas — read `references/canvas.md`
302	
303	The canvas is the single source of truth for static UI mockups: the `surface`
304	locks each artboard's footprint, mixed surfaces lay out
305	in lanes, annotations are plain-text designer notes anchored by
306	`targetId`/`placement`, and edits are surgical `contentPatches`. Before
307	authoring or editing ANY canvas, artboard, or annotation, READ
308	`references/canvas.md` in this skill directory — it is the single source of truth
309	for canvas/artboard mechanics. Do not author canvas layouts from memory.
310	Canvas artboards use the same HTML wireframe path as document-body
311	`WireframeBlock` screens: author `<Screen surface="..." html={...} />` with a
312	semantic HTML fragment. Do not author fresh kit-tree children such as
313	`<FrameScreen>`, `<Card>`, `<Row>`, or `<Btn>` inside canvas `<Screen>` tags;
314	those are legacy compatibility markup for old plans and produce brittle canvas
315	layouts.
316	
317	## Document quality — read `references/document-quality.md`
318	
319	The document is a serious technical plan, not marketing: outcome-first,
320	prose-first, self-contained, built from the right native blocks, with open
321	questions in a single bottom `question-form` and a pre-handoff visual check.
322	Before authoring the plan document, READ `references/document-quality.md` in this
323	skill directory — it is the single source of truth for the document quality bar.
324	Do not write the document from memory.
325	
326	## Good vs. bad exemplar — read `references/exemplar.md`
327	
328	For a worked example of the bar — a great UI-first plan and `/visual-plan`, plus
329	the anti-patterns to avoid — READ `references/exemplar.md` in this skill
330	directory before authoring a plan.
331	
332	## Tool Guidance
333	
334	- `create-visual-plan`: start one structured visual plan per agent task/run, or
335	  import an existing text plan by passing `planText`; `content` may include no
336	  visual surface, canvas only, or canvas + prototype.
337	- `create-ui-plan`: start a UI-first plan when the work is primarily product UI.
338	- `create-prototype-plan`: start a prototype-first plan with a functional top
339	  review surface.
340	- `create-plan-design`: start a full-fidelity branded Design-tab plan with an
341	  optional matching Prototype tab.
342	- `convert-visual-plan-to-prototype`: convert an existing HTML wireframe canvas
343	  into a prototype plan.
344	- `create-visual-questions`: use only when the user explicitly asks for a visual
345	  intake questionnaire, not as `/visual-plan` preflight.
346	- `update-visual-plan`: revise content, status, or comments with targeted
347	  `contentPatches` (see Core Workflow step 6).
348	- `read-visual-plan-source`: read the normalized plan as `plan.mdx`,
349	  optional `canvas.mdx`, optional `.plan-state.json`, and JSON.
350	- `patch-visual-plan-source`: apply granular MDX AST patches by stable block,
351	  artboard, annotation, component, or wireframe-node id.
352	- `import-visual-plan-source`: create or replace a plan from an MDX folder.
353	- `get-visual-plan`: read the current structured plan, exported HTML, and
354	  annotations; it also returns the MDX folder for source workflows.
355	- `get-plan-feedback`: read unconsumed human feedback. Use it frequently; it
356	  returns grouped threads, exact anchor details, expected resolver, and recent
357	  review-event payloads so agents can act only on the comments meant for them.
358	- `get-plan-blocks`: resolve block tags before authoring — do not memorize tags;
359	  call this first to get the authoritative tag names, required fields, and prop
360	  shapes from the live block registry.
361	- `export-visual-plan`: export HTML, Markdown fallback, structured JSON, and MDX
362	  files for repo check-in.
363	
364	When the user critiques a plan's look or structure, fix the renderer or this
365	skill — never hand-edit one stored plan. Turn feedback into better guidance.
366	
367	## Local-Files Privacy Mode
368	
369	Use local-files privacy mode when the user explicitly asks for no DB writes,
370	no hosted Plan database writes, no Plan MCP publish, fully local files, offline/private
371	planning, repo-owned/source-controlled planning artifacts, or when
372	`AGENT_NATIVE_PLANS_MODE=local-files` is set. Also use it when a user or repo
373	policy says a plan must stay under their own brand, domain, source control, or
374	infrastructure. In this mode the plan data must never be sent to the Plan MCP
375	server or Plan app action surface. Schema-only block catalog lookup is allowed
376	because it sends no plan content: use the MCP `get-plan-blocks` tool if it is
377	already available, or run
378	`npx @agent-native/core@latest plan blocks --out plan-blocks.md` and read that
379	file before authoring MDX.
380	
381	The local-files contract is:
382	
383	- Read source context from local files and shell commands only.
384	- Fetch/read the block catalog before writing structured MDX. The
385	  `plan blocks` command calls the public no-auth `get-plan-blocks` route and
386	  writes only registry metadata to disk; use `--format schema` if exact nested
387	  fields are needed. If network access is unavailable, use the bundled
388	  references and rely on `plan local check` / `plan local serve` to catch
389	  invalid tags. For `checklist` and `question-form`, copy the catalog examples
390	  verbatim: checklist items need `id` and `label`; question-form questions need
391	  `id`, `title`, and `mode`; and each option needs `id` and `label`. `plan local
392	  check` validates these required fields against the renderer schema.
393	- Write the plan as a local MDX folder: use `plans/<slug>/` when the user
394	  wants the artifact checked into the repo, or use a repo-ignored/temporary
395	  folder such as `.agent-native/plans/<slug>/` or `/tmp/agent-native-plans/<slug>/`
396	  when it should not be checked in. The folder contains `plan.mdx`, optional
397	  `canvas.mdx`, optional `prototype.mdx`, and optional `.plan-state.json`.
398	- Run `npx @agent-native/core@latest plan local check --dir plans/<slug>`
399	  before serving, then run
400	  `npx @agent-native/core@latest plan local serve --dir plans/<slug> --kind plan --open`.
401	  Report the returned local bridge URL from stdout or `plans/<slug>/.plan-url`.
402	  Treat `.plan-url` as a local token file and do not commit it. The URL opens
403	  the hosted Plan UI but reads from the localhost bridge on this machine, so it
404	  is not shareable across machines. On macOS, `--open` prefers Chromium browsers;
405	  if Safari opens, switch to Chrome/Chromium because Safari can block the hosted
406	  HTTPS page from fetching the HTTP localhost bridge. If the Plan app itself is
407	  running locally with the same `PLAN_LOCAL_DIR`, the `/local-plans/<slug>` route
408	  is also valid.
409	- For headless verification, run
410	  `npx @agent-native/core@latest plan local verify --dir plans/<slug> --kind plan`.
411	  It starts the bridge, checks the private-network preflight and JSON payload,
412	  prints diagnostics, and exits. If the browser hangs on "Loading plan", fetch
413	  the `bridgeUrl` from the verify/serve JSON to read the concrete validation
414	  error.
415	- Do **not** call `create-visual-plan`, `create-ui-plan`,
416	  `create-prototype-plan`, `create-plan-design`, `import-visual-plan-source`,
417	  `update-visual-plan`, `patch-visual-plan-source`, `get-plan-feedback`,
418	  `export-visual-plan`, or any hosted Plan tool for that plan except the
419	  schema-only block catalog lookup above.
420	- Treat feedback as file or chat feedback: update the MDX files directly, rerun
421	  the local bridge command, and summarize the new local bridge URL. Hosted
422	  comments, sharing, history, and publish/export receipts are unavailable until
423	  the user explicitly opts into publishing.
424	
425	Local-files mode prevents plan content from going to the Agent-Native Plan
426	database. It does not by itself make the coding agent's language model local;
427	for that stronger privacy boundary, the host agent/model must also be local or
428	otherwise approved by the user.
429	
430	## Interpreting comment anchors
431	
432	`get-plan-feedback` returns rich anchors — read them before acting on any comment.
433	
434	- **Coordinate frames.** `targetX`/`targetY` are percentages *within* the
435	  element named by `targetSelector`/`targetKind`. Bare `x`/`y` are percentages
436	  of the whole plan document. `canvasX`/`canvasY` are raw board-world pixels on
437	  the design canvas (board size given when available).
438	- **Wireframe pins.** Anchors on wireframes include `targetNodeId` and
439	  `targetNodePath` (e.g. `card > list > listItem "Acme Inc"`) identifying the
440	  exact kit node. Use `targetNodeId` directly with wireframe node patch ops;
441	  use `data-design-id` values from design artboards with
442	  `update-design-element-style`. Prefer the node id/path over raw coordinates;
443	  fall back to coordinates plus the focused screenshot (red ring marks the exact
444	  point) only when no node id is present.
445	- **Text quotes.** Resolve `textQuote` against current prose using
446	  `contextBefore`/`contextAfter` for disambiguation. If `ambiguous: true`, ask
447	  the user — do not guess which occurrence is meant.
448	- **Detached comments.** `get-plan-feedback` flags threads whose quoted text no
449	  longer exists as `detached` (in `detachedThreads`). Reconcile these against
450	  rewritten content — never silently drop them.
451	- **Routing.** `resolutionTarget` is the only routing signal: act on `agent`,
452	  treat `human` as context only. `@mentions` are people to notify, never a
453	  routing signal.
454	- **Two-axis state.** Mark every ingested comment as consumed
455	  (`consumedCommentIds` on `update-visual-plan`). Set `status=resolved` only on
456	  agent-targeted comments you actually addressed; leave human-targeted comments
457	  open.
458	
459	## Visibility & Sharing
460	
461	Use `set-resource-visibility` to change who can see a plan (e.g. public, login,
462	or org-scoped). Use `share-resource` to grant specific users or roles access
463	by email or role. Gate visibility before sharing any plan that covers
464	unreleased or private work — default to the narrowest scope that meets the
465	review need.
466	
467	## Setup & Authentication
468	
469	There are two ways into Plans.
470	
471	**Coding agent (CLI).** Install once with the Agent-Native CLI. The command
472	installs the Plans skills, registers the hosted Plans MCP connector, and runs
473	auth/setup for the selected local client(s) in the same step (a one-time browser
474	sign-in at setup — this is intended), so the first tool call in that client does
475	not hit an OAuth wall:
476	
477	```bash
478	npx @agent-native/core@latest skills add visual-plan
479	```
480	
481	After that, `/visual-plan` and `/visual-recap` are the two installed slash
482	commands. The other planning modes (`create-ui-plan`, `create-prototype-plan`,
483	`create-plan-design`, `create-visual-questions`) are MCP tools reachable from
484	`/visual-plan`, not separate slash commands. Pass `--no-connect` to register
485	the connector without authenticating, then run
486	`npx @agent-native/core@latest connect https://plan.agent-native.com --client all`
487	whenever you are ready, or choose a narrower `--client`. Auth and MCP tool
488	loading are per client config/session.
489	
490	**Browser (people you share with).** Open the Plans editor and create & edit
491	with no sign-up — you work as a guest. Sign in only when you want to save or
492	share; signing in claims the plans you made as a guest into your account.
493	
494	Sharing and commenting require an account: public/shared plans are viewable by
495	anyone with the link, but commenting on them needs an agent-native account.
496	
497	For fully offline, no-account use, run the Plans app locally and sync plans to
498	your repo as MDX. This local mode is a separate advanced path, not the default
499	hosted flow.
500	
501	If a Plans tool returns `needs auth`, `Unauthorized`, or `Session terminated`,
502	do not keep retrying the tool. Stop and give the user the reconnect step for the
503	client they are using: Codex/Codex Desktop should run
504	`npx -y @agent-native/core@latest reconnect https://plan.agent-native.com --client codex`
505	and start a new Codex session; Claude Code should run `/mcp` and choose
506	Authenticate/Reconnect for the plan connector, or run the reconnect command with
507	`--client claude-code` and restart Claude. To refresh every local client config
508	that already has the Plan entry, use `--client all`, then restart/reload each
509	client. Reconnect re-authenticates WITHOUT reinstalling and finds the entry by
510	URL regardless of connector name. Never reinstall from scratch just to fix auth.
511	Continue once the connector is available.
512	
513	Hosted default: connect `https://plan.agent-native.com/_agent-native/mcp`. Do
514	not put shared secrets in skill files.
515

```text
def enumerate_playlist(playlist_url: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Return {playlist_id, title, videos: [{video_id, url, title, duration}]}.

    Tries yt-dlp flat extraction first (fast, no downloads, includes per-entry
    durations), then falls back to pytube. A plain video URL is treated as a
    single-episode playlist.
    """
    try:
        import yt_dlp
        opts = {"quiet": True, "no_warnings": True, "extract_flat": "in_playlist", "skip_download": True}
        with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
            # process=False skips format resolution entirely — metadata only,
            # works for playlists AND single videos even on older yt-dlp
            info = ydl.extract_info(playlist_url, download=False, process=False)
        entries = info.get("entries")
        entries = list(entries) if entries is not None else [info]  # generator when process=False
        videos = []
        for e in entries:
            if not e:
                continue
            vid = e.get("id")
            if not vid:
                continue
            videos.append({
                "video_id": vid,
                "url": f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}",
                "title": e.get("title") or vid,
                "duration": e.get("duration"),
                "uploader": e.get("uploader") or e.get("channel"),
            })
        return {
            "playlist_id": info.get("id") or "unknown",
            "title": info.get("title") or playlist_url,
            "videos": videos,
        }
    except Exception as e:
```

23	
24	## Block headings
25	
26	Blocks do not take a `title`. To give a block a heading, place a `rich-text` block whose markdown is a `###` (h3) heading directly above the block. Those headings are real, inline-editable, and appear in the document outline — unlike the legacy block `title` field, which renders as a small muted label and cannot be edited in place. This includes the bottom Open Questions form: put an `### Open Questions` heading above the `question-form` block rather than titling it. The `title` field still renders for older plans, but do not set it on new blocks.
27	
28	## Authoring rules
29	
30	**Diagrams**: use `diagram` blocks with `data.html`/`data.css`. Use renderer-owned classes: `.diagram-panel`, `.diagram-card`, `.diagram-node`, `.diagram-box`, `.diagram-pill`, `.diagram-muted`, plus `data-rough`. Use `--wf-*` CSS tokens for color; never set custom fonts or hard-code hex/rgb/hsl values. Legacy nodes/edges only for tiny previews or true step-by-step flows. Use `mermaid` only when textual grammar is materially clearer than a spatial layout.
31	
32	**Wireframes**: set `data.html` to a semantic HTML fragment; pick a surface (desktop/mobile/popover/panel/browser). The renderer owns theme, footprint/aspect, Excalifont, and rough.js sketch overlay. Use `--wf-*` CSS tokens for any custom color (never hex). Prototype screens use semantic HTML with `data-goto` attributes for navigation.
33	
34	**Visual frames**: `wireframe` and `diagram` data accept `frame: "auto" | "show" | "hide"`. Leave it unset/`auto` when the host context should decide: Plan and recap surfaces default to framed; docs default to unframed. Use `frame: "show"` for standalone product screens, before/after recap comparisons, screenshot-like artifacts, and visuals that need containment from surrounding prose. Use `frame: "hide"` when a docs page, tab, column, card, canvas artboard, or the visual's own internal chrome already supplies the boundary. Hiding the outer frame must not remove inner padding, meaningful card/field/button borders, or the visual's readable structure.
35	
36	**Canvas storyboards**: if the user asks for a canvas, storyboard, wireframe, light storyboard, UI flow, screen flow, product flow, mockup, or visual comparison, the primary artifact must be `content.canvas` / `canvas.mdx` with `DesignBoard` artboards containing `Screen` HTML wireframes. Each canvas `Screen` must carry `html` / `data.html`; never author fresh nested kit-tree children such as `<FrameScreen>`, `<Card>`, `<Row>`, or `<Btn>` inside canvas `<Screen>` tags. Kit trees are old-plan compatibility only and often render worse on the pan/zoom canvas than HTML wireframes. Do not use document-body `diagram` blocks for the primary UI story. Use `diagram` only for architecture, data flow, or implementation mechanics below the canvas, and only after the UI storyboard exists.
37	
38	**Before/After columns**: compose a `columns` block from `<Column>` CHILDREN — never a `columns=` attribute or inline JSON array. Author it as `<Columns><Column label="Before">…child block(s)…</Column><Column label="After">…child block(s)…</Column></Columns>`. Each `<Column>` wraps real nested blocks (e.g. a `Wireframe`); the parser fills in column ids and child-block `data` from that markup, whereas a `columns=` attribute array leaves them missing and FAILS schema validation. For UI state comparisons put one `wireframe` block in each side and label the columns `Before` and `After`; the renderer draws labels as headings and lays narrow surfaces side by side. Never bake Before/After labels inside the wireframe HTML or hand-stack the pair.
39	
40	**MDX prose and component syntax**: write ordinary top-level prose as normal Markdown; it imports as rich-text automatically. Use `<RichText id="...">…</RichText>` only when prose needs explicit metadata such as `title`, `summary`, or `editable`, or when preserving a referenced block id. Every capitalized block component must be self-closing (`<Diagram id="..." data={{ ... }} />`) or have a matching closing tag around children (`<RichText id="...">…</RichText>`). Never write a bare opening tag like `<RichText ...>` as a paragraph; the MDX parser treats it as unclosed JSX and import fails before the plan can render.
41	
42	**Code-bearing blocks**: `code`, `annotated-code`, and `diff` are whitespace-sensitive. Prefer the exact MDX form emitted by the authoring examples / source exporter, where multiline code is encoded as JSON string attributes such as `code={"const x =\\n  y"}`. Static template literals are accepted and preserve indentation, but they must be static strings with no `${...}` interpolation.
43	
44	**File maps**: prefer `annotated-code` blocks (real code + line-anchored notes) grouped in a vertical `tabs` block, one tab per key file. Drop to a plain `code` block only for throwaway snippets with nothing to call out.
45	
46	**Tabs grouping**: use horizontal `TabsBlock` groups for multiple related diffs so each split diff gets full document width.
47	
48	**API endpoints**: keep `api-endpoint` and `openapi-spec` blocks in normal single-column document flow. Use `columns` only for an explicit before/after contract comparison.
49	
50	**Visual fidelity and renderMode**: leave `renderMode` unset or set it to `wireframe` for normal wireframes. “Higher fidelity,” “pixel-accurate,” “polished mockup,” “production-like,” “real design,” or “not a sketch/wireframe” requires `renderMode: "design"`, substantial branded HTML/CSS grounded in the real app, and stable `data-design-id` targets. Put scoped styles in the wireframe/prototype `css` field — never in a `<style>` tag. On an existing plan, update the same plan id with `set-visual-render-mode` plus the upgraded HTML/CSS; do not create a duplicate. The viewer-local Clean toggle is not a fidelity upgrade.`
51	
52	## Authoring examples
53	
54	Copy a working shape from these complete, valid examples instead of inferring one from the JSON schema. Each is generated from a real block and round-trips through the strict source parser, so every required field is present (tab `id`, nested child `data`, checklist item `id`, question-form question/option `id`, api-endpoint `responses[].status`, non-empty `callout` body). Keep block `id`s unique and edit the content; do not drop required fields.

T-048 H0 ("stop the bleeding") is the first slice of Lane A's ingestion-hardening
roadmap. It does not fix corpus correctness — that's H1 (identity/dedup), H2 (the
Neon bridge), H3 (resumable runs), H4 (provenance backfill). H0 fixes the things
that make the *filesystem itself* untrustworthy: a tool-cache directory checked
into the corpus, dead module surface, and an index that has quietly drifted from

<teammate-message teammate_id="t045-mainpy-fixes" color="green" summary="pyright regressions fixed: 39 errors → 0">
Fixed. `pyright main.py` was 39 errors, now 0. Root causes and fixes:

1. **The Optional-narrowing sweep (37 of 39 errors)** — the M1 deferred-import globals (`display`, `kb_service`, `cocoindex_processor`, `ContentAnalysisEngine`, `add_to_knowledge_base`, `process_youtube_url_enhanced`, `process_web_url_enhanced`, `upload_file_to_openai`, `add_processed_content_to_queue`, `web_processor`, `WebContentProcessor`) were left with no type annotation, just `= None`. Pyright infers each one's declared type by unioning every assignment it can see across the module — the `None` initializer plus the real import inside `_import_heavy_dependencies()` — landing on `Optional[<real type>]`. It has no way to know that function's `global` reassignment happens before any call site uses them (that's a runtime guarantee, not something pyright traces across function boundaries), so every `display.print_stage(...)`, `kb_service.kb_crud`, `cocoindex_processor.process_document_knowledge_graph(...)`, etc. got flagged as a possible None access. Fixed by annotating each as `: Any = None` instead of leaving it inferred — `Any` is also the accurate type here, since what's actually bound at runtime is opaque to static analysis (whichever class/function/instance `processing.web_content_processor` / `lib.knowledge_base_service` / `lib.terminal_display` / `lib.cocoindex_integration` / `lib.upstash.queue` happen to export). This one change cleared 37 of the 39 errors in a single pass — no per-call-site asserts or suppressions needed. `main.py:36-58`.

2. **Line 55's `reportAssignmentType`** — was actually a side effect of #1's fix exposing a second problem: `add_processed_content_to_queue`'s fallback (when Upstash isn't configured) was a nested `def` *inside* `_import_heavy_dependencies()`, which is itself an explicit type declaration for that name and conflicted with the module-level `Any` annotation (`reportRedeclaration`, "obscured by a declaration of the same name"). Fixed by pulling the fallback out into a normal top-level function `_queue_not_configured()` and assigning `add_processed_content_to_queue = _queue_not_configured` in the except block — a plain expression assignment, not a competing declaration. `main.py:60-70` (new function), `~135` (assignment site).

3. **PyPDF2 unresolved import** — not caused by my changes; pyright was resolving against the system Python 3.11 (`/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.11`), not this project's `.venv` (Python 3.12, where PyPDF2 is actually installed). There was no `[tool.pyright]` config anywhere in the repo to tell it otherwise. Added one to `apps/disclosure-rag/pyproject.toml` (`venvPath = "."`, `venv = ".venv"`, `pythonVersion = "3.12"`) — this is a real, repo-wide gap (not scoped to main.py) that any file's pyright/Pylance run would have hit.

4. **Line 281's `reportCallIssue`/`reportArgumentType`** — unrelated to the deferred-import pattern: `_STAGE_ICONS.get(stage.get("status"), "❔")` — `stage.get("status")` on a `Dict[str, str]` returns `str | None` without a default, which doesn't match `_STAGE_ICONS.get`'s `str` key parameter. Fixed with `stage.get("status", "")`.

Verified after all fixes: `pyright main.py` → 0 errors/0 warnings. `python -m py_compile main.py` passes. `main.py --help` output byte-identical to before, still ~0.08s (M1 unaffected). `pytest tests/test_postgres_client.py tests/test_main.py tests/test_rag_prompt_pipeline_wiring.py` → 48/48 pass. `--status` and `--dry-run` smoke-tested manually, output unchanged from before this pass. 340	
341	/**
342	 * searchDatabase — the disclosure-mindmap-agent + Prometheus chat search tool.
343	 * Preserves existing interface: { table, searchTerms, searchFields, limit }.
344	 * When `embedding` is provided, runs FTS and pgvector search in parallel and
345	 * fuses them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (scale-invariant), so keyword and
346	 * semantic matches compete on rank agreement rather than raw score magnitude.
347	 */
348	export async function searchDatabase({
349	  table,
350	  searchTerms,
351	  limit = 3,
352	  embedding,
353	}: {
354	  table?: string
355	  searchTerms?: string[]
356	  searchFields?: string[]
357	  limit?: number
358	  embedding?: number[]
359	}): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]> {
360	  if (!searchTerms?.length && !embedding?.length) return []
361	  const query = searchTerms?.join(' ') ?? ''
362	  const pgTable = table ? resolveTable(table.toLowerCase()) : undefined
363	
364	  if (!embedding?.length) {
365	    // FTS only
366	    return pgTable
367	      ? searchTable(pgTable, query, limit)
368	      : searchAll(query, limit)
369	  }
370	
371	  // Pull a deeper candidate pool from each signal than the final limit so RRF
372	  // has rank structure to fuse, then trim to `limit` after fusion.
373	  const pool = Math.max(limit * 3, 10)
374	
375	  const [ftsResults, vecResults] = await Promise.all([
376	    query
377	      ? (pgTable ? searchTable(pgTable, query, pool) : searchAll(query, pool))
378	      : Promise.resolve([] as Record<string, unknown>[]),
379	    pgTable
380	      ? vectorSearch(pgTable, embedding, pool)
381	      : vectorSearchAll(embedding, pool),
382	  ])
383	
384	  return fuseRRF([ftsResults, vecResults], limit)
385	}
```
</details></tool-use>

# ADR 0002 — Temporal Observatory: port GL4SS concepts, do not embed GL4SS

**Status:** Accepted — 2026-08-01
**Context source:** Design conversation (Claude Desktop), captured in [`../vision/TEMPORAL_OBSERVATORY.md`](../vision/TEMPORAL_OBSERVATORY.md)
**Upstream:** [gl4ss.ai](https://gl4ss.ai) · [github.com/elder-plinius/GL4SS](https://github.com/elder-plinius/GL4SS)

## Decision

Do **not** integrate GL4SS as an iframe, a standalone sub-application, or a second globe.

Keep Ultraterrestrial's Mapbox/deck.gl spatial renderer. Port GL4SS's *temporal instrument, reconstruction
engine, archive semantics, journey model, and registered comparison interaction* into a new unified feature
named **Temporal Observatory**.

GL4SS functions as the conceptual and partially reusable time-navigation kernel — not the host application.

## Why not embed

Embedding would leave the platform carrying:

- Two map/globe engines (deck.gl/Mapbox vs. Leaflet + raw Three.js).
- Two competing navigation systems.
- Two persistence models (Postgres/object storage vs. browser IndexedDB).
- A jarring visual transition between "research mode" and "generated history mode."
- Build-system friction (Vite app shell vs. Next.js App Router).

GL4SS's own documentation notes that its browser-local archive **cannot make a shared link reproduce the same
image for another person**. That alone disqualifies IndexedDB as the canonical artifact store for a platform
whose credibility rests on reproducible provenance.

## Corrections to the source analysis

The originating design doc contained several claims about this repo that do not hold. They are corrected here
so they do not become the next entry in CLAUDE.md's "corrected myths" list.

| Claim in source doc | Verified reality (2026-08-01) |
|---|---|
| "Next.js 14 / React 18 application" | **Next.js `^15.5.0`, React `19.2.0`** — `apps/app/package.json` |
| "React-version friction" with GL4SS | **No friction.** GL4SS is React 19; so are we. This is *not* a reason to avoid embedding — the real reasons are the five listed above. |
| "already carries … globe.gl, H3" | **`globe.gl` and `h3-js` are absent** from every `package.json` in the workspace. H3 is available only indirectly via deck.gl's `H3HexagonLayer` (4 usages in `features/sightings`). |
| "Xata/Postgres data access" — keep | **Xata is retired.** Use `@db/postgres` exclusively. Three stale `@db/xata` references remain (`apps/app/src/types/modules.d.ts`, `apps/app/src/features/user/api/save-event.ts`, plus a doc) — out of scope here, worth a cleanup ticket. |
| API "reads complete static GeoJSON files and returns them together" | **Half true, and the useful half is missing.** `sightings-globe.tsx:22` does load a static `/sightings.geojson`. But `/api/disclosure/uap-sightings/route.ts` **already** does year-range querying, `limit`, 10-year batching, and optional stats via `getSightingsByTimeChunk`. The bounded-query foundation exists; the globe simply does not use it. |

**Consequence for sequencing:** the Foundation milestone is smaller than the source doc assumes. It is largely
*wiring the existing bounded API to the globe* and generalizing it, not building bounded querying from nothing.

## Existing assets that shorten the path

Verified present in `apps/app/src/features/sightings/`:

- `useTimeSeriesAnimation.tsx` — precedent for **Flap Playback**.
- `animated-arc-layer.tsx` / `animated-arc-group-layer.tsx` — precedent for the **trajectories layer**.
- deck.gl layer usage already spans `ArcLayer` (20), `GeoJsonLayer` (17), `ScatterplotLayer` (14),
```

It traces back to **ADR 0002** (2026-08-01), which made a real decision: port concepts from the external GL4SS project rather than embed it, keeping Mapbox/deck.gl as the renderer and Postgres/object-storage as the persistence layer instead of GL4SS's browser-local IndexedDB (correctly flagged as disqualifying for a provenance-focused platform).

**What's missing:** it lives entirely at the vision/ADR layer. _**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-5 2026-08-01 22:29:22Z)**_

No nested copies; the sole remaining reference is the read-only `SessionStart` hook. Done.

## Root cause

A `Stop` hook in `/Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/.claude/settings.json` (formerly lines 84–95). It was the only writer — nothing in `.claude/hooks/hooks.json`, `.claude/commands/`, `.claude/skills/`, cron, or any nested `.claude` produces these blocks.

Three separate bugs, exactly as you predicted:

1. **Trigger.** `Stop` fires at the end of *every* assistant turn, not once per session. That's why it kept firing live mid-edit.
2. **Prepend.** It wrote a temp file, then `cat DAILY_WORK_PLAN.md >> "$tmp"; mv "$tmp" DAILY_WORK_PLAN.md` — pushing content down on every turn.
3. **Template.** `echo "_Last agent session: $ts_"` — bash parses `$ts_` as a variable named `ts_` (underscore is a valid identifier character), which is unset, so it expanded to empty. `${ts}_` was intended. That's the always-blank date field.

## What I changed

- **Removed the `Stop` hook block entirely** from `.claude/settings.json`. This is a judgment call you may want to overturn: I did not repair the trigger + `${ts}` template as suggested, because a per-turn automated stamp on a Tier-3 curated doc is wrong regardless of formatting. If you want the logging back, the correct shape is *append* to an untracked path with `${ts}` — say the word and I'll add it. Remaining hook events: `PostToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `PreCompact`. JSON validates. The file is untracked/gitignored, so nothing to commit.
- The `SessionStart` hook still *reads* `DAILY_WORK_PLAN.md` into context — harmless, left alone.
- **Cleaned `DAILY_WORK_PLAN.md`**: 11 junk blocks had accumulated (up from the 3 you saw). Cut lines 1–36 after verifying every line above the `# Daily Work Plan` H1 was pure boilerplate — zero non-junk lines. 258 → 228 lines, all real content preserved. Backup at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-liamellis-Desktop-apps-ultraterrestrial-resurrection/c39ecdfe-e0a1-4204-91c5-c243387ca1fb/scratchpad/DAILY_WORK_PLAN.md.bak`.
- Updated the stale "**Open concern:** ...until that trigger is found" bullet at `DAILY_WORK_PLAN.md:24` to record the resolved root cause.

## What I could not verify — needs one check from you

**I cannot confirm it stays clean.** Claude Code snapshots hook config at session start by design, so your still-running session is likely holding the *old* hook in memory and will probably prepend one more block at the end of your next turn. I'm a subagent — my completion fires `SubagentStop` (not configured), so I can't trigger a `Stop` to self-test.

After your next turn, run:

```
grep -c '^_Last agent session:' DAILY_WORK_PLAN.md
```

If it returns non-zero, restart the session to pick up the new config, then re-truncate. If it returns 0, the fix is live and confirmed.

Two smaller caveats: `git diff --stat` on settings.json was empty because the file is untracked, not because the diff was minimal — the `PostToolUse` prettier hook may have reformatted it, and I have no baseline to prove otherwise (harmless for untracked config). And `daily-plan-reseed` is still listed as an active agent; if it rewrites this file, its version and my truncation could race.

/**
 * Agent Inferences — the analytical-layer overlay table (Vision Phase 1.2,
 * renamed per terminology ruling 2026-07-08).
 *
 * TERMINOLOGY CONTRACT: "claim" is a reserved canonical term in this system —
 * a discrete assertion extracted from SOURCE material (human testimony,
 * documents). What the AI agent produces is an INFERENCE: part of the agent's
 * intellectual apparatus, persisted so the analytical trail is auditable and
 * so it can later support a user's growing research theory. It is NOT
 * evidence and must NEVER feed retrieval, search, or suggestion paths — any
 * future consumer must treat `agent_inferences` as interpretive layer only.
 *
 * Every edge `reasoning` string the mindmap agent writes to the graph is
 * persisted here, so analysis built during a session is recoverable as
 * structure rather than living only in ephemeral SSE messages.
 */
import { getSql } from './client'

export type EvidentiaryState =
  | 'observed'
  | 'corroborated'
  | 'contested'
  | 'inferred'
  | 'speculative'
  | 'resonant'
  | 'unverified'
  | 'disconfirmed'

export interface AgentInferenceRecord {
  id: string
  inference_text: string
  evidentiary_state: EvidentiaryState
  source_record_id: string | null
  source_table: string | null
  target_record_id: string | null
  extracted_by: string
  created_at: string
}

export interface InsertAgentInferenceInput {
  inferenceText: string
  evidentiaryState?: EvidentiaryState
  sourceRecordId?: string | null
  sourceTable?: string | null
  targetRecordId?: string | null
  extractedBy?: string
}

export async function insertAgentInference(
  input: InsertAgentInferenceInput,
): Promise<AgentInferenceRecord> {
  const sql = getSql()
  const rows = (await sql.query(
    `INSERT INTO agent_inferences (
      inference_text, evidentiary_state, source_record_id, source_table,
      target_record_id, extracted_by
    ) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)
    RETURNING *`,
    [
      input.inferenceText,
      input.evidentiaryState ?? 'unverified',
      input.sourceRecordId ?? null,
      input.sourceTable ?? null,
      input.targetRecordId ?? null,
      input.extractedBy ?? 'mindmap-agent',
    ],
  )) as AgentInferenceRecord[]
  return rows[0]
}

### DesignLabUiBrief > What `packages/design-lab` is
## What `packages/design-lab` is

A **prototype + reference archive**, not a publishable app package:

| Asset class | Examples | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Surface HTML | `prototypes/01`–`04` | Fixed artboard concepts for four research instruments |
| Gallery / refs | `prototypes/`, `dossier-art/`, `textures/`, `ui-mockups/` | Materiality + product mock mood board |
| Unfinished | `document-system/` | Specimen + CSS exist but **unfinished** — broken consumer links / no React handoff. See [`document-system/README.md`](./document-system/README.md) |

There is no `package.json`, Storybook, or build. Consumption path is: **read → brief → port into `apps/app`**.

### Design Lab — UI Design Brief > Screen-by-Screen Notes > 1. Living Research Canvas
### 1. Living Research Canvas

- **Hero content:** investigation title + count meta (`entities · relationships · unresolved contradictions`).
- **Board:** rotated paper cards (artifact / government record / org / event / testimony / hypothesis) pinned and thread-linked.
- **Left dock:** layer toggles (all / corroboration / contradictions / hypotheses / verified) + saved views.
- **Right dock:** selected-entity dossier — quote, fact rows, evidentiary weight, AI suggestion panel (dashed / violet register).
- **Tools:** Add Pin, Connect, Run Proximity Analysis, Epistemic overlay pill.
- **Canon corrections:** replace Inter/Georgia chrome with Martian Mono labels + one Special Elite title moment; clipped dossier corner on inspector; redaction-bar loading; drop glow blooms and soft SaaS radii.

### Design Lab — UI Design Brief > Layout / Information Architecture
## Layout / Information Architecture

```
App shell
├── Rail (surface switch: Canvas · Ledger · Observatory · Hypothesis · …)
└── Shell
    ├── Topbar (brand · context · search · sync · identity)
    └── Main viewport (one active instrument)
        ├── Canvas: board + floating docks
        ├── Ledger: 3-column (index · claim · provenance)
        ├── Observatory: map / timeline split
        └── Hypothesis: comparison grid + synthesis column
```

**IA rules**

- Rail switches **instruments**, not marketing pages.
- Global search is a **trace** entry point (⌘K in product), not a separate “search product.”
- Intelligence lives **in records, waypoints, and connections** — not extra sidebars of “insight cards.”
- Live app already uses Zustand `setActiveView()` for canvas views; lab rail should map to those views / overlays, not invent a parallel router taxonomy.

## evidence ledger claim detail layout

### Design Lab — UI Design Brief > Screen-by-Screen Notes > 2. Evidence Ledger
### 2. Evidence Ledger

- **Left:** research index tree (claims, primary sources, testimonies, orgs, hypotheses, contradictions, circular citations) + active filters.
- **Center:** claim statement as H1; working interpretation; **Support** / **Challenge** lanes with source cards; source comparison matrix.
- **Right:** provenance lineage (press office → newspaper → microfilm → OCR) + credibility composition meters + Evidence Agent callout.
- **Language:** “Claim” only for source-extracted assertion (correct here). AI text is inference, never “evidence.”
- **Canon corrections:** remove left accent side-stripes (DESIGN ban); use badge grammar + lane color instead; rename “Credibility model” toward **Evidentiary Weight**.

=== AdminDashboard head ===
'use client'

import type {
  EventsRecord,
  PersonnelRecord,
  TopicsRecord,
  TestimoniesRecord,
  OrganizationsRecord,
} from '@db/postgres'

// Helper to get count from paginated or array response
function getCount<T>(data: T[] | { records: T[] }): number {
  if (Array.isArray(data)) {
    return data.length
  }
  return data?.records?.length || 0
}

interface AdminDashboardProps {
  events: EventsRecord[] | { records: EventsRecord[] }
  keyFigures: PersonnelRecord[] | { records: PersonnelRecord[]; pagination?: unknown }
  topics: TopicsRecord[] | { records: TopicsRecord[] }
  testimonies: TestimoniesRecord[] | { records: TestimoniesRecord[] }
  organizations: OrganizationsRecord[] | { records: OrganizationsRecord[]; pagination?: unknown }
}

export function AdminDashboard({
  events,
  keyFigures,
  topics,
  testimonies,
  organizations,
}: AdminDashboardProps) {
  const eventsCount = getCount(events)
  const keyFiguresCount = getCount(keyFigures)
  const topicsCount = getCount(topics)
  const testimoniesCount = getCount(testimonies)
  const organizationsCount = getCount(organizations)

  return (
    <div className="relative z-10 h-full overflow-y-auto p-8">
      <h1 className="text-3xl font-bold text-white mb-8">Admin Dashboard</h1>

      <div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">
        {/* Events Card */}
        <div className="bg-white/5 backdrop-blur-sm rounded-xl p-6 border border-white/10">
          <h2 className="text-xl font-semibold text-white mb-2">Events</h2>
          <p className="text-4xl font-bold text-purple-400">{eventsCount}</p>
          <p className="text-sm text-gray-400 mt-1">Total events in database</p>
        </div>

        {/* Key Figures Card */}
        <div className="bg-white/5 backdrop-blur-sm rounded-xl p-6 border border-white/10">
          <h2 className="text-xl font-semibold text-white mb-2">Key Figures</h2>
          <p className="text-4xl font-bold text-blue-400">{keyFiguresCount}</p>
          <p className="text-sm text-gray-400 mt-1">Personnel records</p>
        </div>

        {/* Topics Card */}
        <div className="bg-white/5 backdrop-blur-sm rounded-xl p-6 border border-white/10">

'use client'

import '@/features/mindmap/research-canvas/canvas-animations.css'

import {useState} from 'react'
import {GLOSSARY, LAST_SYNCED, TICKETING_SYSTEM, TICKETS, type Status, type Ticket} from './data'

const STATUS_ORDER: {status: Status; label: string; accent: string}[] = [
  {status: 'blocked', label: 'Blocked', accent: 'var(--ut-stamp)'},
  {status: 'in_progress', label: 'In Progress', accent: '#d4a017'},
  {status: 'decision_ready', label: 'Decision Ready', accent: '#9b7bb8'},
  {status: 'open', label: 'Open', accent: 'var(--ut-ink-dim)'},
]

const LANE_LABEL: Record<string, string> = {A: 'Lane A · Corpus & Ingestion', B: 'Lane B · Platform & Experience'}

function LaneTag({lane}: {lane: Ticket['lane']}) {
  if (!lane) return null
  const color = lane === 'A' ? '#d4a017' : '#6bbf7a'
  return (
    <span
      className='ut-mono shrink-0 rounded-sm px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[8px] tracking-[0.12em] uppercase'
      style={{color, border: `1px solid ${color}55`}}
    >
      {lane}
    </span>
  )
}

function TicketCard({t}: {t: Ticket}) {
  return (
    <div
      className='flex flex-col gap-1 border-b px-3 py-2.5 last:border-b-0'
      style={{borderColor: 'var(--ut-line)'}}
    >
      <div className='flex items-start justify-between gap-2'>
        <span className='ut-mono text-[9px] tracking-[0.1em]' style={{color: 'var(--ut-ink-faint)'}}>
          {t.id}
        </span>
        <LaneTag lane={t.lane} />
      </div>
      <p className='text-[12.5px] leading-snug' style={{color: 'var(--ut-paper)'}}>
        {t.title}
      </p>
      {t.note && (
        <p className='text-[10.5px] leading-snug italic' style={{color: 'var(--ut-ink-dim)'}}>
          {t.note}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

.classification-badge {
  /* Positioning */
  position: absolute;
  top: 16px;
  right: 16px;
  z-index: 10;
  
  /* Visual Design */
  display: inline-block;
  padding: 8px 16px;
  font-family: 'Impact', sans-serif;
  font-size: 12px;
  font-weight: 900;
  letter-spacing: 1.5px;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  
  /* Physical Effects */
  transform: rotate(-3deg);
  border: 2px solid var(--classification-border);
  background: var(--classification-color);
  box-shadow: 
    0 3px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2),
    inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2);
  
  /* Authenticity Details */
  filter: contrast(1.1);
  transition: transform 0.2s ease;
}

.classification-badge:hover {
  transform: rotate(-3deg) scale(1.05);
}

function RoadmapStrip({title, steps, current}: {title: string; steps: string[]; current: string}) {
  return (
    <div className='flex flex-col gap-1.5'>
      <p className='ut-mono text-[9px] tracking-[0.14em] uppercase' style={{color: 'var(--ut-ink-faint)'}}>

          const isCurrent = s === current
          const isPast = steps.indexOf(current) > i
          return (
            <div key={s} className='flex items-center gap-1'>
              <span
                className='ut-mono rounded-sm px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[9px]'
                style={{
                  color: isCurrent ? 'var(--ut-void)' : isPast ? 'var(--ut-ink-dim)' : 'var(--ut-ink-faint)',
                  background: isCurrent ? '#d4a017' : 'transparent',
                  border: isCurrent ? 'none' : '1px solid var(--ut-line)',
                }}
              >
                {s}
              </span>
              {i < steps.length - 1 && (
                <span style={{color: 'var(--ut-line)'}}>—</span>
              )}
            </div>
          )
        })}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

## (b) Is there a "team activity" concept? No.

Nothing in these docs describes a team/agent activity view. The concept does not exist in the design canon. What exists are three **adjacent patterns designed for research entities, not people**: the facepile + SYNCED/identity chips, the "Recently Accessed" timestamped strip, and the "AI Suggested Connections" agent-proposal feed. Those are real, reusable visual grammar — but you'd be repurposing them, and the brief's IA rule ("intelligence lives in records and connections — not extra sidebars of insight cards") pushes against a bolted-on feed panel. Also note: `@liveblocks/react` is a dependency but there is no presence/room wiring; live multiplayer is aspirational (`docs/plans/FEATURES.md`).

## (c) Recommendation

The current `board/page.tsx` already independently reinvented the ledger's lane grammar (280px columns, mono uppercase header + count, accent-per-status). Converge it onto `02-evidence-ledger.html` rather than inventing further: adopt `.sourcecard`'s **footer meta row** for per-ticket owner/agent + last-touched, and the **numbered provenance lineage** as the activity-feed row shape. Take the facepile and `SYNCED ⌄` chip from the research-desk mockup into the existing header, beside `RoadmapStrip`.

Two binding constraints from the canon: **no left accent side-stripes** (explicit DESIGN ban — use badge grammar + lane color instead, which the ledger mockup violates and the brief corrects), and **no glow blooms or soft SaaS radii**. Use redaction-bar skeletons for loading. Keep everything on `--ut-*` + `.ut-mono`; don't follow `evidence-layers-panel.tsx` into raw Tailwind colors.

- `.../apps/app/src/features/spacetime/components/evidence-layers-panel.tsx` — a live panel reimplementing the same grammar in **raw Tailwind** (`font-mono`, `bg-black/70`, `accent-amber-300`) instead of `--ut-*`/`ut-mono`. Existing drift not worth repeating.
- `.../apps/app/src/app/board/page.tsx` + `data.ts` — baseline: 280px status columns, mono uppercase header + count, accent per status, `LaneTag`, `RoadmapStrip`, collapsible Done, `GlossaryRail`. `Ticket` is `{id, title, lane, status, note}` — no owner, agent, or timestamp field.

**Not relevant:** `dossier-art/`, `textures/`, `mood-references/`, `gateway/`, `process-refs/` (materiality only); `document-system/` (explicitly unfinished); `docs/vision/UI_INSPIRATION.md` (external Fable demo links — atmospheric, no dashboard content).

## (b) Is there a "team activity" concept? No.

Nothing in these docs describes a team or agent activity view; the concept does not exist in the design canon. What exists are three genuinely adjacent patterns, all designed for **research entities rather than people**: the facepile + SYNCED/identity chips, the "Recently Accessed" timestamped strip, and the "AI Suggested Connections" agent-proposal feed. Reusing them means borrowing visual grammar, not semantics. Note also that the brief's IA rule — "intelligence lives in records, waypoints, and connections, not extra sidebars of insight cards" — argues against a bolted-on feed panel. And `@liveblocks/react` is in `package.json` but has no room/presence wiring, so live multiplayer is aspirational (`docs/plans/FEATURES.md`).

## (c) Recommendation

The current board already independently reinvented the ledger's lane grammar. Converge it onto `02-evidence-ledger.html` rather than inventing further: adopt `.sourcecard`'s footer meta row to carry per-ticket owner/agent and last-touched, and use the numbered provenance-lineage list as the activity-feed row shape. Lift the facepile and `SYNCED ⌄` chip from the research-desk mockup into the existing header beside `RoadmapStrip`. Adding activity requires extending `Ticket` with owner/agent and timestamp fields — the current shape can't express it.

Two binding constraints from the canon: **no left accent side-stripes** (explicit DESIGN ban — use badge grammar plus lane color; the ledger mockup violates this and the brief corrects it), and **no glow blooms or soft SaaS radii**. Use redaction-bar skeletons for loading, and keep everything on `--ut-*` + `.ut-mono`.

## (b) Is there a "team activity" concept? No.

Nothing in these docs describes a team or agent activity view; the concept does not exist in the design canon. What exists are three genuinely adjacent patterns, all designed for **research entities rather than people**: the facepile + SYNCED/identity chips, the "Recently Accessed" timestamped strip, and the "AI Suggested Connections" agent-proposal feed. Reusing them means borrowing visual grammar, not semantics. \```
GET /api/board/activity
→ [{ slug, label, lastActiveAt, relativeTime }, ...]
\```

Parse the filename slug into a human label (strip the ISO timestamp prefix,

actual complaint.

<Callout id="ia-tension" tone="decision">

The design brief states: *"intelligence lives in records, waypoints, and
connections — not extra sidebars of insight cards."* That's a direct argument
against bolting a separate activity-feed panel onto the board. This plan follows
it: **activity renders as a row inside each existing `TicketCard`**, not as a
new sidebar or panel. The facepile/`SYNCED ⌄` chip pattern from the research-desk
mockup is reserved for the page header only (global "board last polled at…"
indicator), not per-card — keeping the per-card surface to one added row.

</Callout>

## Risks

<Callout id="risk-slug-quality" tone="risk">

`.specstory/history/` filenames are auto-generated from the first user message
in a session — slugs can be vague ("give-me-a-rough", "where-did-we-leave-off")
or collide across unrelated sessions on the same ticket. This is acceptable for
v1 (better than nothing) but don't over-promise precision — the activity row
says "someone was active," not "this specific agent worked this specific
ticket." No reliable ticket-to-session mapping exists today.

</Callout>

<Callout id="risk-fs-read-cost" tone="warning">

524 files today, growing daily. A naive full-directory stat on every poll is
fine now; if this becomes a real bottleneck later, cache the listing and only
stat files newer than the last poll. Not a v1 concern — noted so it isn't
rediscovered as a surprise.

</Callout>
